> **bminney:** I couldn't see an appimage anywhere? Has it been taken down?

It's still up, but it's attached to a pre-release, so the "Latest" release page doesn't show it. It's an alpha: it uses CUDA for nvidia GPUs with fallback to Vulkan for AMD/Intel GPUs. Since, runpod only hosts NVIDIA GPUs, I've only tested it on NVIDIA so far, so reports from AMD or Intel machines would help a lot.

> **bazdesh** One thing though, I had issues running it, had an error with the packaged libjpeg, had to run with
```
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libjpeg.so.8 ./Fotufilm-Linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

If you can share the actual error, it could really help me in debugging the issue. The appimage bundles libjpeg. A version mismatch is my best guess.

Both projects are following the same physical chain (spectral exposure, development, printing), so a lot of the controls end up looking alike. The implementations are quite different though (Swift and Halide on the GPU, versus Python), so merging the code isn't really practical. Sharing datasheet traces is, and I'd still like to do that.

*Still working on full comparison. Will post soon.*

[quote="bazdesh, post:25, topic:60539"]
/usr/lib/libtiff.so.6: undefined symbol: jpeg12_write_raw_data, version LIBJPEG_8.0
[/quote]

Thanks, that pinned it down. The AppImage carried Ubuntu's libjpeg-turbo 2.1 but used your system's libtiff, and Arch builds libtiff against libjpeg-turbo 3, which added the 12-bit jpeg12_* functions. The image now carries libjpeg-turbo 3 instead. I reproduced your error on Arch with the old image and checked the new one starts there and on Ubuntu 24.04. It's in the 1.11 beta, so you shouldn't need the LD_PRELOAD any more:
https://github.com/DhaliwalX/fotufilm-engine/releases/tag/v1.11-beta

Hi @DhaliwalX, and thanks for sharing Fotufilm!

I've been trying different film stocks, including Kodak Portra 400 and Gold 200, and to my eye the output often looks a little muted, almost as if there's a slight grey veil over the image.

I'd like a slightly clearer, cleaner look with better tonal separation, while preserving each stock's character. What would you recommend adjusting first: the output medium or conversion mode, exposure, paper grade, or something in the input preparation?

Is this impression related to the default rendering, and do you have a recommended starting point for achieving this kind of look?

Hey @oude , thanks for trying it!

I am suspecting that this is most likely coming from the defaults. In the desktop app, the negative-to-postive conversion in the Output tab opens on Auto Levels by default, which simulates the lab scanner behaviour. This lifts the shadows and flattens contrast.

Switch it to Graded Print and set Scan Exposure yourself; This is most film character preserving output. Paper Grade basically adjusts the contrast. If you are using the browser app, then these films open on Ektacolor Edge paper, whose black reads as dark grey on screen. Try Digital Reference there with Graded print, or you can pull Shadows Level down a little.

Otherwise if this still does not fix it, could you share a frame and your settings so I can take a look?

I have been also investigating this issue lately more often. So with updates this will hopefully get resolved for the defaults as well.

Thanks @Vnz for the report. It's fixed on the latest main.

I also have an update on Fotufilm vs spektrafilm. I got a real roll of Gold 200 and shot a few scenes on both film and digital (a Sony A7C II for the digital frames and for scanning the film).

Methodology:
1. The film and digital frames are aligned as closely as possible. I had no tripod, so there is slight misalignment.
2. I scanned the film with a SmallRig RM120, whose channels sit at roughly blue ≈455 nm, green ≈522 nm and red ≈625 nm (±5 nm). These are estimates, derived from the A7C II's [spectral response data](https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/rawtoaces-data/blob/main/data/camera/Sony_ILCE-7CM2_380_780_5.json).
3. Both simulations were stopped at the negative to keep the comparison as fair as possible.
4. All negatives, real and simulated, were then printed through Fotufilm's Digital Reference output on Graded Print, with identical settings.

Frame 1 (spektrafilm, Fotufilm, real):
[grid]
![frame13-spektrafilm|690x455](upload://A2AXGxlCGjl9Jo9iWBGLUQ1Fl9g.jpeg)
![frame13-fotufilm|690x455](upload://xZ5tAFubZUqJ9Qe5KJUyhgU2jGk.jpeg)
![frame13-real|690x455](upload://1QBDr7B0rShFlahUJnbwPB8yCs9.jpeg)
[/grid]

The real film is warmer in the shadows, and neither simulation matches it. Fotufilm is closer to the real Gold 200 than spektrafilm here.

Frame 2:
[grid]
![frame17-spektrafilm|542x1000](upload://ditrRdK99hzJlO0QF78LYQJgxRB.jpeg)
![frame17-fotufilm|542x1000](upload://w01K00eeaiUy3ibQMZeHP6G8Zsa.jpeg)
![frame17-real|542x1000](upload://s6PflYijUavPYKx6Argu3pAlnVz.jpeg)
[/grid]

Both simulations miss the greens: the real film turns them olive. The yellows are very close across all three, with Fotufilm closest to the film.

Frame 3:
[grid]
![frame18-spektrafilm|652x1000](upload://h1bjrjyx4mRIaM863HFIGvDM2Lx.jpeg)
![frame18-fotufilm|652x1000](upload://bupUE6QSAYOwbWfrUMS8ftQ805q.jpeg)
![frame18-real|652x1000](upload://4iy4XntNpmxLFrxjMkXlhBPKHDj.jpeg)
[/grid]

Here spektrafilm is closer to the film in the sky but misses the flower colour completely. Fotufilm turns the sky cyan but matches the flower.

I also tried running Fotufilm's Gold 200 profile inside spektrafilm:
[grid]
![frame18-spkff|652x1000](upload://caHGlDQhiJOwUvVqUSpKTIk4DHz.jpeg)
![frame17-spkff|542x1000](upload://dAiJUeyl9cVNDUskvWdGoYJkicO.jpeg)
![frame13-spkff|690x455](upload://n7WhwzEfItaIFpcCdd4z9nTP2xu.jpeg)
[/grid]

With that profile, spektrafilm still oversaturates the colours. With its DIR couplers turned off, spektrafilm matches Fotufilm's colours and moves closer to the film, so spektrafilm's default couplers seem a bit too strong.
